title: NLTM Hamiltonians from gauged sheaf quantum locally testable codes
authors: Fuchuan Wei, Zhengyi Han, Zimu Li, Zi-Wen Liu
abstract: Understanding the complexity of low-energy quantum states is a central problem in quantum complexity theory and many-body physics. Here we prove the no low-energy trivial magic (NLTM) conjecture, constructing a family of local Hamiltonians for which every state within a positive energy density window requires circuit depth $Ω(\log n)$ to prepare from arbitrary stabilizer state that may themselves be highly entangled. Notably, our result is intrinsic in the sense that the same Hamiltonian family and energy density threshold apply to arbitrary qudit stabilizer inputs with any bounded local dimensions. Our construction builds on non-Abelian gauged sheaf codes obtained using the cup product structure on good quantum locally testable codes. We establish constant operator soundness for the associated Hamiltonians, enabling their protected logical structure to constrain all states at sufficiently low energy density. By excluding shallow stabilizer-based classical witnesses, Our result substantially strengthens NLTS and advances our understanding of low-energy complexity relevant to quantum PCP.
summary: This work establishes a strong lower bound on the circuit depth required to prepare low-energy quantum states associated with specific local Hamiltonians. By constructing these Hamiltonians from advanced quantum codes, the authors prove that the complexity scales logarithmically with system size, significantly strengthening existing conjectures in quantum complexity theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the complexity of preparing low-energy quantum states governed by local Hamiltonians, connecting this to the quantum PCP conjecture.
main_result: They prove the Intrinsic NLTM Theorem, showing that for a constructed family of Hamiltonians, any low-energy state requires a circuit depth of $\Omega(\log n)$ to prepare from arbitrary stabilizer states.
method: The proof constructs Hamiltonians from non-Abelian gauged sheaf codes and uses arithmetic obstructions derived from the ground state dimension to establish the lower bound on circuit depth.
model_or_system: The model involves local Hamiltonians ($H = \sum h_i$) acting on qudits, whose low-energy states are analyzed in the context of quantum error correction codes (specifically, gauged sheaf codes).
key_observables: Magic circuit complexity ($C_{	ext{magic}}(ho)$), energy density ($	ext{Tr}(Hho)/m_n$), and circuit depth.
important_parameters: System size ($n$), local dimensions ($d_v$), and the energy density window (positive).
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the existence of good quantum locally testable codes and the ability to bound projections related to the code structure.
figures_summary: Figure 1 distinguishes between different types of 'No Low-Energy Trivial Magic' (NLTM) constraints: NLTS, Binary NLTM, and the intrinsic qudit case.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the complexity problem, constructing the specific Hamiltonian family using sheaf theory, and then proving the lower bound on the preparation circuit depth by establishing a contradiction based on code theory.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, concrete example of a quantum complexity barrier ($\Omega(\log n)$ depth) that cannot be circumvented by simply using larger local dimensions or more complex stabilizer inputs, which is crucial for understanding quantum computation limits.
